key_insight: LLMs can answer recorded facts correctly yet mishandle missing information when the required closure assumption changes.
engineering_relevance: AI agents need explicit rules for when missing information means unknown versus false, especially when completeness varies by source or scope.
method: Test each base scenario under open-world (OWA), closed-world (CWA), and local closed-world (LCWA) assumptions.
Change only the treatment of missing information; require correct answers across all closure variants.
Extend evaluation to agent action choice, source scope, and updates.
evidence_signal: Across 960 instances and replicated runs, overall accuracy ranged from 71.18% to 99.86%, while core switch accuracy on scenarios whose gold labels change with the closure rule ranged from 18.23% to 99.31%.
watch_item: Aggregate accuracy can conceal closure failures; inspect assumption-specific results, particularly LCWA.
paper_title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions
